answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can tie each identity to a refundable stake that is slashed when peers prove duplicate or fake work, so creating many fake agents costs real capital rather than free keystrokes. At its zenith, trust flows across a mesa of verified history: only identities with attested useful contributions earn weight, while a trellis of independent peer endorsements cross-checks each claim before rewards release. Newcomers start with low weight and earn more slowly, so a swarm of fresh clones cannot outvote established agents or drain the pool.
